note: Darrell Caldwell, leader of the Stinc Team. His mumbled, sideways 'nervous music' flow ('Mr. Get Out the Way') made him LA's most original voice of the late 2010s. He was prosecuted on gang-conspiracy charges built partly on his lyrics, acquitted of murder, released in 2020, and stabbed to death backstage at a Los Angeles festival in December 2021, aged 28.

pow.t: A Jail House Interview With Drakeo the Ruler

note: Jason Jackson from the Jordan Downs projects. Half-sung, wobbly, endlessly prolific; The Wolf of Grape Street (2018) came out days before he began a prison sentence. He kept releasing music from inside and came home in 2022.

pow.t: The Grapes of Wrath: 03 Greedo Drops a Classic

note: Ermias Asghedom built an independent empire out of the Marathon Clothing store on Slauson and Crenshaw, selling his Crenshaw mixtape for $100 a copy in 2013. Victory Lap (2018) was nominated for a Grammy. He was shot dead outside his store in March 2019.

pow.t: Hussle and Motivate: In Memory of Nipsey Hussle (1985-2019)

note: Kendrick Duckworth first rapped as K.Dot on Top Dawg Entertainment mixtapes. good kid, m.A.A.d city (2012) and To Pimp a Butterfly (2015) followed; DAMN. won him the Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2018, a first for a rapper.

pow.t: Tuesday Throwback: A Kendrick Lamar Interview from 2007

clips.t: All The Stars (From "Black Panther: The Album")

note: Quincy Hanley, a Black Hippy member and Hoover Crip turned TDE star. Habits & Contradictions (2012) and Oxymoron (2014) made his yelp and his bucket hat famous.

pow.t: Riding Around South Central With ScHoolboy Q

note: Herbert Stevens IV, the Black Hippy member most likely to bring up the Illuminati. Control System (2012) is his cult classic; childhood Stevens-Johnson syndrome left him with his trademark dark glasses.

pow.t: Abstract Asshole: Ab-Soul's "Control System"

note: Johnny McKinzie from Nickerson Gardens, the first artist Top Dawg Entertainment signed. Redemption (2018) and the Grammy-winning 'King's Dead' came a decade after his debut single.
Vincent Staples came up around Odd Future and Earl Sweatshirt. Summertime '06 (2015), a double album about his teenage summer in Ramona Park, made him rap's driest, funniest pessimist.

pow.t: "I Don’t Know if I Wanna be Forever": An Interview with Vince Staples

note: Keenon Jackson. Built on DJ Mustard's ratchet beats, My Krazy Life (2014) is the definitive LA party-rap record of its decade. 'FDT' (2016) became a protest anthem.

pow.t: The Return Of The Gangsta: YG’s Still Brazy

note: Dominic Hunn, a self-released star with his own OPM label. From the Westside with Love (2010) and its sequels made him the laid-back voice of independent LA rap at the start of the blog era.

pow.t: The Rolexes and Deep Rolodexes of Dom Kennedy

note: Thebe Kgositsile, son of the South African poet Keorapetse Kgositsile. His Odd Future mixtape Earl (2010) went viral while his mother had him at a reform school in Samoa. Some Rap Songs (2018) remade the underground in his image.

pow.t: Earl Sweatshirt, Lost and Found: An Investigative Report by Doc Zeus

note: Tyler Okonma, ringleader of Odd Future. He went from the shock-rap of Bastard (2009) and 'Yonkers' to Grammy-winning albums IGOR (2019) and Call Me If You Get Lost (2021).

pow.t: Tyler, The Creator Interviewed for CRWN

note: Michael Eagle II, a Chicago native who came up in LA's Project Blowed scene. He called his work 'art rap'; Brick Body Kids Still Daydream (2017) is about the Robert Taylor Homes where he grew up.

pow.t: Some Incredible Sadness and Some Loneliness - An Interview with Open Mike Eagle & Serengeti (Cavanaugh)

clips.t: Trying to Remember What I Aimed At
The Many Hustles of my Lonely Time Traveling Uncle

note: Regan Farquhar, son of the screenwriter who co-wrote Krush Groove. A Project Blowed fixture with a tongue-twisting, jazz-scat speed; Temporary Forever (2002) and Fear of a Black Tangent (2005) are underground touchstones.

pow.t: But You Knew That, Come On: Busdriver "Perfect Hair"

clips.t: Can’t You tell I’m a Sociopath
Kill Your Employer (Recreational Paranoia Is the Sport of Now)

note: David Blake, a producer-rapper who played most of the instruments himself. Quik Is the Name (1991) and Safe + Sound (1995) built G-funk-adjacent records with live funk musicianship few could match.

pow.t: An Interview With DJ Quik and JasonMartin (FKA Problem)

note: Ricardo Brown, Philadelphia-born and Dogg Pound half with Daz Dillinger. One of the sharpest technicians on The Chronic and Doggystyle; Kuruption! (1998) was his solo debut.

pow.t: I’ll Be Rapping Until I’m 100: An Interview with Kurupt

note: Dejuan Walker, a pimp-rap stylist with a high, sing-song wheedle. Street Gospel (1997), produced by DJ Quik, is his classic.

pow.t: The Return of Suga Free

clips.t: I'd Rather Give You My Bitch

note: Garrett Gonzalez, co-founder of Shoreline Mafia with Fenix Flexin, whose woozy party records ('Musty', 'Bands') ran LA in the late 2010s. He went solo after the group's split in 2021.

pow.t: The High Priests: Shoreline Mafia Make a Triumphant Return

note: Matthew Burdette, producer, rapper and singer. No Love Lost (2020) blended melodic rap and R&B, and 'Chosen' with Tyga and Ty Dolla $ign went platinum.

pow.t: Act Like You Know: An Interview with Blxst

note: O'Shea Jackson wrote much of N.W.A's Straight Outta Compton, then left over money. AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted (1990) and Death Certificate (1991) are as furious as West Coast rap gets.

pow.t: Who is Ice Cube?

clips.t: Gangsta Rap Made Me Do It
You Know How We Do It

note: Calvin Broadus, introduced on Dr. Dre's The Chronic. Doggystyle (1993) was the first debut album to enter the Billboard 200 at No. 1; that drawl is G-funk's signature.

pow.t: Fallin' Asleep on Death Row: Snoop Dogg's Lost Sessions

note: Earl Stevens, the Bay's great slang inventor, independent from the start through his family's Sick Wid It label. Rappers everywhere borrowed his phrases; he's still releasing records four decades on.

pow.t: An Interview with B-Legit & E-40

note: Andre Hicks, Vallejo's party-rap prophet and founder of Thizz Entertainment. He recorded an album over the prison phone in the '90s and later invented the 'thizz face'. He was shot dead in Kansas City in 2004.

pow.t: Who Killed Mac Dre?

note: Andre Adams, once Dre Dog, from the Fillmore. An underground king of San Francisco with an eccentric, punchline-dense delivery; Tears of a Clown (1999) is the cult favourite.

pow.t: A Beginner's Guide to Andre Nickatina, San Francisco's Underground King

note: Brandon McCartney, from the teen group The Pack ('Vans', 2006). Solo, he posted thousands of songs to hundreds of MySpace pages, invented 'based' positivity, and became an internet religion.

Larry Hill, a Bay rapper whose cheerful hustler-health-food motivational raps (organic juice, 6 a.m. jogs) slowly became a national cult. The Great Escape (2023) with The Alchemist was a breakthrough.

pow.t: "I Want Money and I Want to be Happy": An Interview with Larry June

note: Vallejo's 'Big Tymin'' (2015) hit made Nef the Pharaoh E-40's Sick Wid It protégé. His slurring, high-pitched delivery owes something to Mac Dre.

pow.t: An Interview with Nef the Pharaoh

note: Timothy Patterson from Oak Park, Sacramento. Grief-heavy street rap, released at a furious independent rate; Gangland Landlord (2018) went national.

pow.t: "Sacramento is Where I Call Home": An Interview with Mozzy

note: Robert Green, a Bay gangsta-rap pioneer who started in Too $hort's orbit. Spice 1 (1992) and 187 He Wrote (1993) are among the hardest records the Bay ever made.

pow.t: Veteran from the West: Spice 1 Remains The O.G.

note: Brad Jordan of the Geto Boys and Rap-A-Lot. Heavy, haunted storytelling about death and paranoia; peers routinely name him one of the greatest of all time.

pow.t: A People's History of Hip-Hop: Scarface-Old Joy

note: Chad Butler, producer and loud half of UGK with Bun B. A country-soul arranger and a quote machine, he died in 2007. 'Big Pimpin'' and 'Int'l Players Anthem' carry his verses.
Bernard Freeman, the precise, steady half of UGK. While Pimp C was in prison, Bun's features kept the 'Free Pimp C' campaign alive; Trill (2005) went top 10.

pow.t: LA Times Article Plus Interview With Bun B

note: Joseph McVey from Missouri City, a Screwed Up Click member who sings as much as he raps. Let the Truth Be Told (2005) is lonely, hard and gorgeous.
Marcus Edwards, a Screwed Up Click original. His freestyle 'Pimp tha Pen' on DJ Screw's tapes became a Houston anthem.
Stayve Thomas from Houston's Northside. He founded Boss Hogg Outlawz; Already Platinum (2005), produced by the Neptunes, hit the top 10.

pow.t: Like Bawses: How Slim Thug and Rick Ross Do It

note: Devin Copeland, Rap-A-Lot's mellow, laughing stoner philosopher. Dr. Dre put him on 'Fuck You' (2001); Just Tryin' ta Live (2002) is his warmest record.

pow.t: Question in the Form of An Answer: An Interview With Devin the Dude

note: Emekwanem Biosah Jr., the son of Nigerian immigrants, from Houston's Southwest. Detailed, deadpan family crime stories; Brandon Banks (2019) is named after his father's alias.

pow.t: "I Might Get Killed for Being Black and Wearing a Seat Belt": An Interview with Maxo Kream

note: Megan Pete from South Park, Houston, who went viral with freestyles in college. Fever (2019), 'Savage' and 'WAP' made her a star; her mother, Holly Thomas, rapped as Holly-Wood.

Fredrick Tipton from Gary, Indiana, dropped by Interscope before he had released anything. POW was on his mixtapes early; Piñata (2014) and Bandana (2019) with Madlib, and Alfredo (2020) with The Alchemist, followed.

pow.t: A (Semi) Definitive Ranking of Every Freddie Gibbs Album

note: Rahkiem Meyer, a former Flipmode member. Marcberg (2010), which he self-produced, launched the drumless, loop-heavy pimp-noir style a decade of underground rap followed.

pow.t: "I’m Always Trying to Keep Pushing Myself": An Interview with Roc Marciano

note: Daniel Sewell from Detroit's Dexter-Linwood. A yelping, unhinged voice and a decade of drug confession: XXX (2011) and Atrocity Exhibition (2016) are both cult landmarks.

pow.t: Back For the First Time: "Hot Soup" and The Old Danny Brown

clips.t: Tell Me What I Don't Know

note: Alvin Worthy, co-founder of Griselda Records with his brother Conway and cousin Benny the Butcher. His Hitler Wears Hermes tapes made Buffalo the underground's capital.

pow.t: "I LOVE FLY STREET SHIT": AN INTERVIEW WITH WESTSIDE GUNN

clips.t: Why I do em Like that

note: Demond Price, Griselda co-founder. Shot in the head and neck in 2012, he raps with partial facial paralysis; From King to a God (2020) is his peak.
James Jones from Detroit, an Alchemist collaborator since My 1st Chemistry Set (2013). Flat, exact drug-trade detail; he released four albums in 2020 alone.

pow.t: "Not Everybody is Comfortable in Their Own Skin" : An Interview With Boldy James

note: A Washington D.C.-born, Zimbabwe-raised New Yorker who runs the label Backwoodz Studioz. Solo (Hiding Places, Aethiopes) and in Armand Hammer with Elucid, he's the underground's most literary pen.

pow.t: Question in the Form of An Answer: An Interview With Billy Woods

note: Adolph Thornton Jr., Chicago-born, Memphis-raised, independent through his Paper Route Empire label. He survived a 2017 shooting in Charlotte and was killed in Memphis in November 2021.

pow.t: Give Young Dolph His Flowers While He Can Still Smell Them

clips.t: What u see is what u get

note: Patrick Houston, Juicy J's older brother and a Three 6 Mafia affiliate. Mista Don't Play (2001) and 'Chickenhead' are Memphis classics.
Raymond Sweeney from Detroit's East Side. A calm, conversational flow and the leader of Detroit's current street-rap wave; FACE (2022) broke him nationally.

pow.t: "You Have to Go Through Different Shit in Life to Make Music:" An Interview with Babyface Ray
